name: Direct lateral (Hardinge) approach to the proximal femur (periprosthetic)
corridor: Transgluteal split of gluteus medius and vastus lateralis raising an anterior myofascial sleeve to reach the anterior hip capsule and proximal femur

positioning.text: Position in lateral decubitus or supine with the greater trochanter accessible and the limb free.

surface_landmarks.text: Center the incision over the greater trochanter with its proximal end directed slightly posteriorly.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal incision through skin and subcutaneous tissue down to the fascia lata over the trochanter.

superficial_interval.text: Split the fascia lata and release the anterior third of gluteus medius and minimus while preserving their posterior femoral attachment.

deep_interval.text: Elevate the anterior fibers of vastus lateralis from the anterior femur in continuity with the abductors to create an anterior myofascial sleeve, then perform an anterior longitudinal capsulotomy with a proximal transverse limb.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, gluteus medius and minimus anteriorly, vastus lateralis, and the anterior hip capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The superior gluteal nerve, which crosses 3 to 5 cm proximal to the tip of the greater trochanter, limits proximal splitting of the abductors and its injury causes abductor weakness.

danger_zones.text: Splitting the gluteus medius more than 3 to 5 cm above the trochanteric tip is the danger zone for the superior gluteal nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not extend the abductor split proximally beyond the safe margin and avoid excessive proximal retraction on the medius.

exposure.text: Gentle external rotation, and dislocation if needed, exposes the femoral head, neck, and proximal femur.

limitations.text: Violation of the abductor mechanism can cause a postoperative limp, and heterotopic ossification is common.

indications.text: Excellent for periprosthetic fractures of the proximal femur and usable for revision arthroplasty and hemiarthroplasty.

closure.text: Reattach the anterior myofascial sleeve securely with heavy sutures, close in layers, and consider a subfascial drain given the blood loss risk.

complications.text: Complications include superior gluteal nerve injury with abductor weakness and limp, heterotopic ossification, and wound problems.

procedure_applications.condition: A periprosthetic proximal femoral fracture needs lateral exposure of the hip and femur
Hemiarthroplasty is performed through a direct lateral exposure

questions.question: How far above the greater trochanter does the superior gluteal nerve cross?
questions.answer: About 3 to 5 cm proximal to the tip of the greater trochanter.

questions.question: What is created by elevating the anterior abductors with vastus lateralis?
What is the characteristic late complication of the direct lateral approach?
questions.answer: Abductor weakness with a postoperative limp.
